newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai Vacuum announces share ownership changes.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai Vacuum announces share ownership changes.

text.p: Shanghai Vacuum and Electron Devices Co Ltd announced on Thursday that the ownership of all its state shares had been transferred to Shanghai Video and Audio Electric (Group) Co.

A statement by the company's board of directors said that the former owner of the state shares, Shanghai Electric Meters (Group) Co, a subsidiary of the Shanghai city government, had withdrawn from the company.
The statement did not give the price, or any other details of the ownership changes and company officials were not immediately available for comment.
Shanghai Vacuum has a total of 237.8391 million state shares, making up 44.78 percent of the firm's 531.0876 million outstanding shares.
The transfer makes Shanghai Video and Audio Electric (Group) Co by far the biggest shareholder in Shanghai Vacuum.
A report in the Shanghai Securities News on Thursday said Shanghai Video and Audio Electric (Group) Co had recently been selected by the State Council, the cabinet, as a "key enterprise".
According, the city government had approved making the group an independent entity under the direct control of the city's Economic Commission, the newspaper said.

The group was formerly wholly owned by Shanghai Electric Meters (Group) Co, a susidiary of the city government, but has now become a shareholding company with its former owner just one of the shareholders, the newspaper said.

The other three shareholders of the group are Shanghai Automobile Industrial Corp, Shanghai Broadcasting, Film and Televsion Development Corp and Shanghai industrial holdings Co Ltd, a subsidiary of the city government listed in Hong Kong.
The newspaper did not give a breakdown of the shareholding.
The group is mainly a producer and trader of video and audio equipment including television sets and video cameras.
Shanghai Vaccum is a television display tube maker.

"The transfer of Shanghai Vacuum's shares to the group will promote the cooperation of the two companies in producing televisions sets as well as their display tubes," the newspaper said. "It wil also enhance the competitiveness of Shanghai's television industry."
Shanghai Vacuum reported a profit of 121.08 million yuan in 1995 and an interim of 3.71 million yuan in mid-1996.
The company's A and B shares listed on the Shanghai stock exchange closed at the 10 percent limit-up on Wednesday.
The Shanghai city government is encouraging healthy state enterprises to acquire stakes in struggling listed firms to help improve their performance.
